input: Label and organize all the spice jars alphabetically

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many jars and whether mixed spices, duplicates, or nearly-empty jars are included determines the scale and complexity of the task.
Whether this is for one person or a shared household affects labeling style and how obvious/accessible the system needs to be.
The storage location (drawer, rack, cabinet, countertop) determines what organizational format makes alphabetizing practical and visible.
Budget and available materials affect whether the user buys new uniform jars, a rack, or label-making tools vs. working with what they have.
Knowing if the labels already exist or need to be made (handwritten, printed, label maker) determines the immediate first step.
The user may want labels on the lid, front, or side — and may prefer a minimalist look vs. detailed labels with dates or usage info.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — a quick tidy-up vs. a fully matching, Pinterest-worthy system — sets the right level of effort.

gold.taskTitle: Label and organize spice jars alphabetically
gold.taskDescription: Sort and label all spice jars in alphabetical order so they are easy to find and maintain.

questions.title: How many spice jars do you currently have?
questions.description: Understanding the quantity helps gauge the time and materials needed for the full project.

questions.title: Who else in your household needs to use the spices?
questions.description: Knowing whether others share the space affects how intuitive and visible the labeling system needs to be.

questions.title: Where are the spices currently stored — drawer, rack, cabinet?
questions.description: The storage location shapes which alphabetical format (rows, tiers, single-file) will actually work.

questions.title: Do you want to buy new uniform jars or use what you have?
questions.description: This determines whether budget and a shopping trip are part of the plan or if the task is purely organizational.

questions.title: How will you create the labels — handwritten, printed, label maker?
questions.description: The labeling method is the most immediate action and shapes what tools need to be gathered first.

questions.title: Where on the jar do you want the label — lid, front, or side?
questions.description: Label placement depends on how jars are stored and what is visible at a glance when grabbing a spice.

questions.title: Is the goal a quick functional sort or a fully matching polished display?
questions.description: This defines the effort level and whether aesthetic consistency is a priority alongside alphabetical order.
